correctness.rationale: The two-type functional equations enumerate the object and leaf/parity marks correctly. Eliminating one type shows both marginal Narayana laws. Differentiating both equations once in each mark yields a closed algebraic mixed derivative; exact binomial coefficient extraction gives E[E_n L_n]=n^2/4-n/[4(2n-3)]. With Narayana mean n/2 and variance n(n-2)/[4(2n-3)], the covariance and correlation follow for every integer n>=3. At n=2 both counts are constant and exempt from correlation. Standalone exhaustive tree enumeration at n=2..11 independently passed 113 exact assertions. Finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The parity-class size and number of leaves are natural global statistics on the same random Catalan tree; each follows exactly the same Narayana law, yet their dependence is not fixed by equidistribution. The exact all-n negative covariance and simple correlation -1/(n-2) quantify a genuine finite-size relationship (perfect anticorrelation for n=3, weak but nonzero for n>=4, vanishing correlation and nonvanishing covariance as n grows). This structural dependence formula is beyond a marginal table computation or trivial substitution.
